headline: Two landlord-profit measures rank second-best citywide, neighbor contact reads zero.
summary:
Little Village, Garfield Ridge, North Lawndale, and Archer Heights sit inside Ward 22, on Chicago's Southwest Side. It lands 39th citywide, with a combined score of 34.84. A caveat attaches to most of what gets measured here too, 163 of the 180 rankings this ward carries.

The strongest numbers touch on housing costs and one measure of air quality. Two related estimates put the share of rent that ends up as landlord profit among the lowest anywhere in Chicago, whether the estimate starts from a property's assessed value or its last sale price. Ozone levels also rank 2nd best in the city. The weakest numbers describe how much neighbors interact with each other. Modeled estimates put the ward last citywide both for residents who trade favors with neighbors monthly and for those who talk with neighbors monthly. The ward also sits near the bottom on two other environmental measures, the city's cumulative Environmental Justice index and a toxic-release index. Ozone measures one pollutant, not the ward's overall environmental burden.
reading_the_rankings: Start with the ward's number one ranking for menu spending on surveillance cameras. Between the thirteenth-best ward and the thirty-eighth on this measure, the spread is zero points, so this first-place finish rests on a difference too small to matter. The two neighbor-connection measures at the bottom, both ranked 50th, come from a model built on a civic engagement survey and census data, not a count of who actually traded a favor or a conversation with a neighbor in this ward. Wards with comparable populations tend to land on similar modeled numbers here, and the source calls the estimate low confidence. The environmental numbers cut two ways. The ward ranks 2nd best on ozone but near the bottom on the city's broader Environmental Justice index and a toxic-release measure. Census tracts and the ward map were drawn for different purposes and do not line up, so part of what these figures count may really belong to a neighboring ward.

news.headline: Garfield Ridge resident crafts neighborhood's first community framework plan
news.note: A recent UIC graduate built Garfield Ridge 2050, a 25-year community plan based on 216 resident survey responses, backed by Ald. Rodriguez and Ald. Tabares.
